openings.claim: A slot-mounted strip pocket with a swinging face gate could retain either plate and permit gloved removal.
openings.delta: Replace magnet-dependent holding with contact boundaries: three strips constrain nonworking sides; the fourth pivots over a nonworking face region. Use bolts in existing slots, cork at contacts, and a releasable wire closure.
openings.prediction: Unlike magnetic holding, geometric restraint should not weaken with the spare plate. Defeat: displacement exceeds 1 mm, gloved removal/return exceeds sixty seconds, or any constraint is breached.
openings.probe: Before fabrication, map slots and clearance with ruler; proceed only if strips, M4 hardware and gate sweep fit. Configuration A: stationary wire closure. Run three twenty-stroke tests and three removal/return checks; final run uses spare and gloves. Mark and measure initial/final position.
assumptions: Slot dimensions, permissible strip footprint, gate stiffness and stroke loads are unknown. Eighty minutes may be insufficient. No forbidden alteration is permitted.

openings.claim: Hypothesized closing loop: mechanism (oblique wire closure) → demand (stroke force transmitted into attempted plate displacement) → response (displacement tensions wire and rotates gate) → mechanism (greater gate compression and friction).
openings.delta: Change the closure carrier from a stationary anchor to a removable wire loop around a nonworking plate corner, routed to pull the gate closed. Nearest rival: ordinary fixed-preload friction plus the same pocket.
openings.prediction: Linked closure should increase measured resistance after equal initial loading; stationary closure should not. Equal increases or absent gate response show no detected return influence. Defeat: tension loosens the gate, requires over 1 mm travel, or compromises removal.
openings.probe: Configuration B shares A geometry. Remove the response→mechanism edge by restoring A stationary closure, preserving geometric retention. Match initial gate pull force and initial 3 N plate demand using the scale; compare gate position/resistance. Give B three runs/checks, final spare/gloves, within the shared cap.
assumptions: Return influence is unsupported. Routing, force matching within scale resolution, sufficient submillimetre response and gloved loop release require demonstration.

assessment: Two configurations only. Reject either before strokes if its resource or clearance conditions fail; a time cap alone establishes no feasible informative test.
